# One customer and four invoices: three in a state `unapply-payment` and
# `unlink` have to refuse for a different reason — never posted, posted but
# never paid, posted and paid twice with no selector — and one posted and paid
# once, which both commands take a payment off without being told which.
#
# The paid one is there so a refusal can be told from a book with nothing in
# it — a command that says "no payments to unapply" about every invoice in the
# book is not answering, and the third invoice is the control that says the
# other two answers are about those two invoices.
#
# `Liabilities:Owed Back` is the account a payment split takes: money received
# that is no longer applied to an invoice is something you may owe back, and
# `--to` has no defensible default.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_saying_why_no_payment_came_off.py, which
# runs every one of these states against both commands.
2026-01-01 commodity CAD
	mnemonic: "CAD"
	fullname: "Canadian Dollar"
	namespace: "CURRENCY"
	fraction: 100
2026-01-01 open Income
	type: Income
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Income:Sales
	type: Income
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Accounts Receivable
	type: Accounts Receivable
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Liabilities
	type: Liability
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Liabilities:Owed Back
	type: Liability
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"

customer "C-UNAPPLY"
	name: "Unapply Customer"
	currency: CAD

invoice "INV-DRAFT"
	customer_id: "C-UNAPPLY"
	currency: CAD
	date_opened: 2026-01-01
	entry:
		date: 2026-01-01
		description: "Never posted"
		account: "Income:Sales"
		quantity: 1
		price: 100
		taxable: false
		tax_included: false

invoice "INV-UNPAID"
	customer_id: "C-UNAPPLY"
	currency: CAD
	date_opened: 2026-01-01
	entry:
		date: 2026-01-01
		description: "Posted, never paid"
		account: "Income:Sales"
		quantity: 1
		price: 100
		taxable: false
		tax_included: false
	posted:
		date: 2026-01-01
		due: 2026-01-31
		ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable"
		memo: "Invoice INV-UNPAID"
		accumulate: true

invoice "INV-PAID"
	customer_id: "C-UNAPPLY"
	currency: CAD
	date_opened: 2026-01-01
	entry:
		date: 2026-01-01
		description: "Posted and paid"
		account: "Income:Sales"
		quantity: 1
		price: 100
		taxable: false
		tax_included: false
	posted:
		date: 2026-01-01
		due: 2026-01-31
		ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable"
		memo: "Invoice INV-PAID"
		accumulate: true
	payment:
		date: 2026-01-15
		amount: 100
		bank_account: "Assets:Bank"
		memo: "Paid in full"

# A fourth: posted and paid twice, in two instalments. Neither command may
# guess which payment a bare run means, so this is the record that reaches
# `need_selector` — the status whose whole job is to say what to type next,
# and the one no book in the suite could produce before.
invoice "INV-TWICE"
	customer_id: "C-UNAPPLY"
	currency: CAD
	date_opened: 2026-01-01
	entry:
		date: 2026-01-01
		description: "Posted and paid in two instalments"
		account: "Income:Sales"
		quantity: 1
		price: 100
		taxable: false
		tax_included: false
	posted:
		date: 2026-01-01
		due: 2026-01-31
		ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable"
		memo: "Invoice INV-TWICE"
		accumulate: true
	payment:
		date: 2026-01-15
		amount: 60
		bank_account: "Assets:Bank"
		memo: "First instalment"
	payment:
		date: 2026-01-20
		amount: 40
		bank_account: "Assets:Bank"
		memo: "Second instalment"

# A fifth: paid in two instalments of which only one is a whole number of
# dollars. `--all` on it, onto an account that counts whole dollars, has to
# refuse — and refuse *both*, having written neither. One instalment alone
# could be stated there, so a run that worked payment by payment would take
# the 60.00 off and then fail on the 40.50, leaving the record half undone.
#
# The total is 100.50 for that reason: where the total is whole, either both
# instalments are whole or neither is, and the case cannot arise.
invoice "INV-PART-WHOLE"
	customer_id: "C-UNAPPLY"
	currency: CAD
	date_opened: 2026-01-01
	entry:
		date: 2026-01-01
		description: "Posted and paid in a whole part and a part with cents"
		account: "Income:Sales"
		quantity: 1
		price: 100.50
		taxable: false
		tax_included: false
	posted:
		date: 2026-01-01
		due: 2026-01-31
		ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable"
		memo: "Invoice INV-PART-WHOLE"
		accumulate: true
	payment:
		date: 2026-01-15
		amount: 60
		bank_account: "Assets:Bank"
		memo: "Whole instalment"
	payment:
		date: 2026-01-20
		amount: 40.50
		bank_account: "Assets:Bank"
		memo: "Instalment with cents"
